intro.p: Six items from the war page of the Keijō Nippō, the Japanese-language daily of Seoul, of 14 October 1924: telegrams of 11–12 October from the Shanhai Pass front of the Second Zhili–Fengtian War, on the Fengtian wounded, the wounding of Guo Songling, the Zhili fleet, Wu Peifu's arrival at the front and a plot against his train.

The transcription keeps the paper's characters and its furigana, in the historical kana spelling of the time. Chinese names are given in the translation in their Japanese readings, as the paper's readers read them; each Persons and Places entry gives the pinyin.

ja.head: 奉天軍の負傷多數
ja.subhead: 醫師の不足補充準備中
ja.p: 奉天電報目下もくか城內じゃうないの衛戍病院ゑいじゅびゃうゐんに收容しうようされ居ゐる負傷者ふしゃうしゃは五百六七十名ごひゃくろくしちじふめいで此外このほか二百名にひゃくめいあり輕傷者けいしゃうしゃは尚なほ戰線せんせんにある由よし
今度こんどの戰爭せんさうで最もっとも奮鬪ふんとうしたのは第二だいに、六ろくの兩りゃう旅りょにて彼等かれらは決死隊けっしたいを組織そしきして手てに手榴彈しゅりうだんを携たづさへて悲愴ひさうなる肉彈戰にくだんせんを爲なしたる爲ため最大多數さいだいたすうの負傷者ふしゃうしゃを出いだし城內じゃうない收容者しうようしゃは殆ほとんどその全部ぜんぶが兩旅りゃうりょの兵士へいしである
現在げんざい戰線せんせんに派遣はけんせる支那しな軍醫ぐんいは五百餘名ごひゃくよめいに達たっするも尚なほ不足ふそくにて滿鐵まんてつや赤十字せきじふじ方面はうめんより醫師いし其他そのたの材料ざいれうに就つき補充ほじゅうの準備中じゅんびちうである

en.head: Many wounded in the Hōten army
en.subhead: Shortage of doctors; reinforcements in preparation
en.p: 【Hōten telegram】The wounded now housed in the garrison hospital within the city walls number five hundred and sixty or seventy, and there are two hundred more besides; the lightly wounded are reported to be still at the front.

In the present war the hardest fighting fell to the Second and Sixth Brigades: they formed death squads and, grenades in hand, fought a grim battle of human bullets, and so produced the greatest number of wounded; almost all of those housed in the city are soldiers of these two brigades.

The Chinese army doctors now sent to the front number more than five hundred but are still too few, and preparations are being made to bring in doctors and other supplies from the South Manchuria Railway and the Red Cross.

ja.head: 奉軍副司令負傷
ja.p: 奉天十二日發電奉天軍ほうてんぐん第三軍だいさんぐん副司令ふくしれい第二だいに旅長りょちゃう郭鐘齡くわくしょうれいの戰死說せんしせつあるが氏しは石門子せきもんしの占領戰せんりゃうせんに奮戰ふんせんして脚部きゃくぶに貫通銃傷くわんつうじうしゃうを受うけ目下もくか錦州きんしうで治療中ちれうちうであると

en.head: Hōten deputy commander wounded
en.p: 【Hōten, the 12th】There is a report that Kaku Shōrei, deputy commander of the Third Army of the Hōten army and commander of its Second Brigade, has been killed in action; but he fought hard in the battle for Sekimonshi, took a bullet through the leg, and is now under treatment at Kinshū.

ja.head: 渤海艦隊出動
ja.p: 青島十二日發電渤海艦隊ぼっかいかんたいの肇永翔てうえいしゃうの二隻にせきは十日とをか青島ちんたうを拔錨ばつべうした一方いっぱう秦皇島しんくわうたうの二艦にかんも出動しゅつどうすべく陸戰隊りくせんたい千五百名せんごひゃくめいの外出ぐわいしゅつを禁きんじ出動命令しゅつどうめいれいを俟まつてゐる

en.head: The Bokkai Fleet puts out
en.p: 【Chintao, the 12th】Two ships of the Bokkai Fleet, the Chōwa and the Eishō, weighed anchor at Chintao on the 10th; the two ships at Shinkōtō are also to put out, and with shore leave stopped for their fifteen hundred marines they await the order to sail.

ja.head: 吳佩孚山海關著
ja.p: 天津十二日發電直隸軍ちょくれいぐん總司令そうしれい吳佩孚ごはいふ將軍しゃうぐんは十二日じふににち午前六時ごぜんろくじ山海關さんかいくわんに到着たうちゃくした

en.head: Go Haifu arrives at Sankaikan
en.p: 【Tenshin, the 12th】General Go Haifu, commander-in-chief of the Chokurei army, arrived at Sankaikan at six in the morning of the 12th.

ja.head: 列車顛覆計畫
ja.p: 北京十一日發電十一日じふいちにち午前ごぜん吳佩孚ごはいふ氏しの搭乘たふじょうせる列車れっしゃが天津てんしん驛えきを通過つうくわせんとする際さい前方ぜんぱう線路上せんろじゃうに電氣仕掛でんきじかけの爆彈ばくだんが裝置さうちしてあるのを一露西亞人いちろしあじんが發見はっけん急報きふはうしたので辛からくも事ことなきを得えた

en.head: Plot to derail a train
en.p: 【Pekin, the 11th】On the morning of the 11th, as the train carrying Go Haifu was about to pass through Tenshin Station, a Russian found an electrically fired bomb planted on the line ahead and gave the alarm, and so a disaster was narrowly avoided.

ja.head: 側面攻擊
ja.p: 奉天發電十二日じふににち朝あさ著電ちゃくでんに依よれば山海關さんかいくわん第一線だいいっせんは皆みな陷落かんらくしたが所

en.head: Flank attack
en.subhead: The Chokurei army fights hard to hold on
en.p: 【Hōten telegram】By a telegram received on the morning of the 12th, the whole first line at Sankaikan has fallen, but —

notes.interp: The datelines give the place and the day a telegram was sent; the days are of October 1924. Names are given in their Japanese readings, as the paper's readers read them; the pinyin is in the Persons and Places entries. 奉天 Hōten is Fengtian, the Mukden of the Western press of the day and the seat of the Fengtian clique.
城內: inside the walled city, that is Hōten (Fengtian), from which the telegram was sent.
五百六七十名: five hundred and sixty-odd to seventy-odd.
由: the hearsay marker; the sentence reports what is said of the lightly wounded.
肉彈戰: a close assault in which the men themselves are the projectiles, a phrase of the Japanese press since the Russo-Japanese War.
奉天十二日發電: sent from Hōten (Fengtian) on the 12th.
郭鐘齡: the paper's writing of 郭松齡, Kaku Shōrei (Guo Songling in pinyin).
石門子 Sekimonshi: the Shimenzhai 石門寨 of the Chinese accounts, in the hills north-west of Shanhai Pass.
肇永翔: the cruisers Chōwa 肇和 and Eishō 永翔 (Zhaohe and Yongxiang in pinyin), their names run together.
天津驛 Tenshin Station: 驛, here the railway station.
所: the item breaks off at the foot of the column; the clipping ends here.
